title: Power Automate: AI-assisted UI automation repair in the desktop flow designer
summary: The briefing accurately describes the documented preview, its licensing and the repair workflow. The admin path matches Microsoft Learn, and the briefing explicitly reports the conflicting guidance on control scope rather than treating either account as definitive.

claims.where: summary; What's changing; Risk assessment; rationale: risk
claims.claim: An eligible selector failure prompts the maker to capture the intended UI element.
claims.quote: When an eligible selector-related failure occurs, the system prompts you to capture the target element and its current selector.

claims.claim: The system proposes a new selector after the maker captures the element.
claims.quote: The maker recaptures the intended UI element. The system analyzes the failing selector and the newly captured selector. AI generates a suggested selector designed to be more resilient.

claims.claim: The maker can review the proposed selector.
claims.quote: Review, edit, and test the proposed selector.

claims.claim: The maker can edit the proposed selector.
claims.quote: Review, edit, and test the proposed selector.

claims.claim: The maker can test the proposed selector.
claims.quote: Review, edit, and test the proposed selector.

claims.claim: The maker can accept the proposed selector.
claims.quote: Accept the selector, recapture the UI element to repeat the process, or skip the suggestion.

claims.claim: The maker can recapture the element instead of accepting the suggestion.
claims.quote: Accept the selector, recapture the UI element to repeat the process, or skip the suggestion.

claims.claim: The maker can skip a suggested repair.
claims.quote: Accept the selector, recapture the UI element to repeat the process, or skip the suggestion.

claims.where: What's changing; Cost and licensing; Scope
claims.claim: Microsoft Learn documents AI-assisted UI automation repair as a preview.
claims.quote: This is a preview feature.

claims.claim: The feature requires Power Automate for desktop version 2.70 or later.
claims.quote: You need version 2.70 or higher for Power Automate for desktop.

claims.claim: Application or web-page UI changes can cause selector failures that require maintenance.
claims.quote: Flows with UI and web automation actions often require maintenance when: Desktop applications or web pages change their UI structure. Existing selectors no longer uniquely identify the intended element.

claims.where: Why it matters; Risk assessment: Data exposure
claims.claim: The feature analyzes the failing selector as an input to its repair proposal.
claims.quote: The system analyzes the failing selector and the newly captured selector.

claims.where: Why it matters; Risk assessment: Data exposure
claims.claim: The feature also analyzes the newly captured selector of the intended UI element.
claims.quote: The feature analyzes the failing selector together with a newly captured selector of the same UI element and proposes a more resilient selector that makers can review, test, and apply.

claims.where: Why it matters; Governance guidance: After rollout
claims.claim: Applied selector changes become permanently saved when the maker saves the flow.
claims.quote: Any selector changes you apply during an AI-assisted run (either incomplete or completed successfully) temporarily store in the flow. The changes are permanently saved when you save the flow, as is the case with any other edits in the flow.

claims.where: front matter: defaultState; Why it matters; rationale: risk
claims.claim: The initial state of the repair feature's required environment setting is not explicitly stated.
claims.quote: Searched: "AI-assisted UI automation repair" "default" "enabled"; "AI-assisted UI automation repair" "enabled by default" "Copilot". Read repair, Copilot overview and Copilot hub pages: the overview gives a broader tenant default, not the repair setting's environment default.

claims.claim: The broader Copilot in Power Automate overview says Copilot is on by default.
claims.quote: If a region has GPUs (UK, Australia, US, India), Microsoft turns on Copilot by default.

claims.claim: The Copilot overview describes disabling Copilot at tenant level and says environment-level support is unavailable.
claims.quote: In this scenario, an admin needs to contact support and they use a PowerShell script to turn it off only at tenant level. Environment level support isn't available.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Security & identity; Scope; rationale: risk; rationale: impact
claims.claim: AI-assisted UI automation repair is a maker debugging capability available only through the desktop flow designer.
claims.quote: AI-assisted UI automation repair is a debugging capability, available only through the flow designer. It doesn't automatically repair selectors during unattended or attended runtime execution.

claims.claim: The documentation describes no new identity or permission model for AI-assisted UI automation repair.
claims.quote: Searched: "AI-assisted UI automation repair" identity permissions security. Read the repair article, its prerequisites, desktop Copilot guidance and desktop governance guidance; no repair-specific new identity or permission model was described.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Autonomy & actions; rationale: risk
claims.claim: Applying a repair requires user review and approval rather than autonomous modification of the flow.
claims.quote: Requires user review and approval before it applies selector changes. Doesn't automatically modify flows without user interaction.

claims.claim: Skipping a suggestion without error handling stops the AI-assisted debug run.
claims.quote: If you skip the suggestion and no error handling is in place, the run throws an error and the AI-assisted debugging run stops.

claims.claim: Accepting a selector changes the affected flow action.
claims.quote: If the maker accepts the suggested selector, it's added to the selectors list of the affected element, so that the action is updated accordingly and the flow can continue to run.

claims.where: front matter: licensing; Cost and licensing; Scope
claims.claim: The documented preview is available for organization premium accounts.
claims.quote: AI-assisted UI automation repair in Power Automate for desktop is currently available for organization premium accounts at no extra cost.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.model; licensing.notes; Cost and licensing; rationale: cost
claims.claim: The preview is included at no extra cost for those organization premium accounts.
claims.quote: AI-assisted UI automation repair in Power Automate for desktop is currently available for organization premium accounts at no extra cost.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing
claims.claim: Preview usage might be subject to service limits or changes.
claims.quote: Usage might be subject to service limits or changes.

claims.where: Cost and licensing; Governance guidance; Governance controls; rationale: risk
claims.claim: AI-assisted UI automation repair requires Copilot in Power Automate to be enabled.
claims.quote: Under the Power Automate section, select Copilot in Power Automate, and then enable the On check box in the displayed pane.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing; rationale: cost; Open questions
claims.claim: General availability pricing and licensing for this feature are not yet published.
claims.quote: Searched: "AI-assisted UI automation repair" "general availability" licensing pricing credits. Read repair preview pricing and Power Automate licensing search excerpts; found preview no-extra-cost terms but no feature-specific GA price or licence terms.

claims.claim: The documented Power Platform admin center path is Copilot > Settings > Power Automate > Copilot in Power Automate > On.
claims.quote: In Power Platform admin center, go to Copilot > Settings. Under the Power Automate section, select Copilot in Power Automate, and then enable the On check box in the displayed pane.

claims.claim: The Copilot hub documents environment-level configuration of its product settings, as reported alongside conflicting tenant-level guidance.
claims.quote: The Settings page displays settings grouped by product. Some settings span across Power Platform and appear at the top in the Power Platform section. You can configure settings at the environment level, with most settings also configurable through environment groups and rules.

claims.where: controls[0].api; Governance controls table and prose
claims.claim: An API or scripting equivalent for this environment-scoped Copilot in Power Automate setting is not yet documented.
claims.quote: Searched: "Copilot in Power Automate" setting PowerShell Set-TenantSettings Power Platform API pac admin environment; separate API and pac admin queries. Read repair, hub and list-tenantsettings; disableCopilot is documented for cloud flows, not this environment repair prerequisite.

claims.where: controls[1]; Governance controls table; Open questions
claims.claim: No dedicated environment admin UI or API switch specific to designer AI-assisted repair is documented beyond the shared Copilot setting.
claims.quote: Searched: "AI-assisted UI automation repair" admin disable switch configuration API. Read repair configuration, Copilot hub, desktop governance and tenant settings; found the shared Copilot prerequisite and separate runtime controls, not a dedicated designer-repair admin switch.

claims.claim: The Copilot hub says most of its settings can also be configured through environment groups and rules.
claims.quote: You can configure settings at the environment level, with most settings also configurable through environment groups and rules.

claims.claim: The desktop governance page directs administrators wanting to prevent all Copilot capability use to contact Microsoft Support.
claims.quote: To prevent your users from using any copilot capability contact Microsoft Customer Support to disable all copilot functionality in your tenant.

claims.claim: The required Copilot prerequisite is shared with other AI-powered Power Automate capabilities.
claims.quote: AI-assisted UI automation repair relies on generative AI models and requires the same Copilot prerequisite as other AI-powered capabilities in Power Automate:

claims.claim: Runtime repair has its own configuration flag distinct from this designer debug experience.
claims.quote: Find the Repair at runtime setting for the desired run mode (attended and unattended) under the Desktop flow repair at runtime configuration setting in the Power Platform admin center.

claims.claim: Self-healing is a separately enabled runtime capability rather than designer AI-assisted repair.
claims.quote: Self-healing is a runtime-only capability. It applies to console and cloud (attended and unattended) runs and has no effect during designer runs.

claims.claim: The Copilot overview connects Copilot availability in regions without GPUs to cross-geo data sharing.
claims.quote: If a region doesn't have GPUs (everywhere else except sovereign clouds), Microsoft turns on Copilot by default by toggling on the cross-geo data sharing.

claims.claim: The desktop Copilot page names a Copilot feedback tenant setting.
claims.quote: As a Power Platform admin, you can prevent users from sending Copilot feedback to Microsoft by using the "Copilot feedback" tenant setting.

claims.claim: The desktop governance page instead names disableSurveyFeedback in its Copilot-related feedback guidance.
claims.quote: As a Power Platform admin you can prevent users from sending feedback to Microsoft by disabling the disableSurveyFeedback tenant setting.

claims.claim: Microsoft does not establish that the Copilot feedback label and disableSurveyFeedback refer to the same setting.
claims.quote: Searched: "Copilot feedback" "disableSurveyFeedback" Power Automate. Read desktop Copilot, governance, tenant-settings and list-tenantsettings; the latter separately describes disableSurveyFeedback as NPS feedback and disableCopilotFeedback as Power Apps Copilot feedback.

claims.claim: The documented shared Copilot setting is not documented as a maker-group switch for this repair feature.
claims.quote: Searched: "AI-assisted UI automation repair" "environment" "group". Read repair configuration and Copilot hub settings; these document environment configuration, not maker-group targeting for designer repair. The hub's user-targeting table covers model-driven apps.

controlChecks.governs: Copilot in Power Automate for an environment
